title: Deutsch–Jozsa: four inputs, then the general case
objectives: Work through a two-input-bit promised example.
Derive the all-zero amplitude and explain the promise.
prerequisites: Chapters 5–7: Hadamard interference, joint states, XOR oracle action, phase kickback and bit ordering.

quizzes.question: Which two-input table violates the constant-or-balanced promise?
feedback: It has two ones and is balanced.
Correct: it has one one, so is neither constant nor balanced.

quizzes.question: Under the promise and ideal circuit, what does any nonzero input readout mean?
options: The entire truth table is known
feedback: Correct: constant functions produce only the all-zero label.
Constant-one phase is global and still yields zero.
Only the required class is guaranteed.
